components.name: The Window
components.description: The glass IS the window: edge to edge, no bezel, no radius, no room around it, with the vignette and the grille as fixed layers over the whole viewport.

narrative.overview:
This is not a web page dressed as a monitor. It is what the monitor shows. The whole window is the tube, a phosphor field whose edges darken and bow, and inside it a teletext service with exactly one subscriber: a numbered page index, a dated log, four keyed destinations, and a block-mosaic wordmark built out of solid cells. Every mark on the screen is made of the same stuff — the eight inks a broadcast teletext decoder had, none of them pure, laid on phosphor black.

The curvature lives in the glass, not in the signal: a vignette that falls off in a curve, an aperture grille and scanlines across the whole window, phosphor glow on the type, and a trapezoid of less than half a degree on the content block. A displacement filter was tried and rejected — it bends what you see and leaves the hit box where it was, so every link became a target you could not click.

The density is deliberately low but the grid is strict: everything sits in a fixed-pitch character cell, set at 11-17px depending on how big the tube is. The window is the frame, not the page. Where a modern site would scroll a document, this one shows one screenful and, when a list is longer than the glass, scrolls inside it the way a terminal does.
keyCharacteristics: The glass is the whole window; the content is a centred 118ch column with slack for the bowing.
Eight teletext inks, none pure, plus a dimmed phosphor white for prose.
Curvature in the glass: vignette, grille and scanlines, plus a sub-degree trapezoid the transform can carry without moving the hit boxes away from the paint.
Aperture grille in vertical RGB stripes and horizontal scanlines, above the signal.
Every word in a bitmap gothic; every numeral and the page number in a dot matrix.
Zero JavaScript, zero cookies, zero third-party requests.
Fixed size on the desk; only the subpages scroll, inside the glass.

rules.name: The Eight Inks Rule
rules.body: Only the eight teletext colours plus a dimmed phosphor white may appear. A colour outside that set is a decoder that never existed.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Ink Rule
rules.body: Nothing reaches purity. The black is blue-black, the white is phosphor-tinted, and every saturated ink stops short of the primaries. Pure #000, #fff, #00ff00, #ff0000 and #0000ff are forbidden.

rules.name: The Blue Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Blue (#3c6cff) is a fill and a frame, never a body colour: on phosphor black it does not reach AA contrast, so it never carries reading.

rules.name: The Once-Magenta Rule
rules.body: Magenta appears in exactly one place in the whole site: the magenta route key. Anywhere else it is a bug.

rules.name: The Character Cell Rule
rules.body: Every word sits in a fixed-pitch cell and the layout is measured in characters — ch for columns, em for rhythm. A proportionally-set word anywhere in this site breaks the screen.

rules.name: The Flush Mosaic Rule
rules.body: The wordmark sets line-height: 1 on purpose: its rows of solid blocks must touch, because the leading is the artwork. This is the only place in the system where leading is allowed under 1.3, and it is text rather than an image so that it scales and selects.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow to imply it sits above the page, nothing glows, and nothing wraps the glass: the tube is the window and the phosphor is the only light.

rules.name: The Grille-Above Rule
rules.body: Aperture stripes and scanlines always sit above the content, never behind it, at low alpha. Below the content they become a background pattern and the screen stops being glass.

dos: Do keep the warp on the signal alone, and let the grille and vignette stay flat on the glass.
Do size type in cqi so the character grid tracks the tube, not the window.
Do give every quantity Doto and every word DotGothic16.
Do spend yellow on structure, cyan on reading, green on open, red on closed, and magenta exactly once.
Do label a date with what it is — the repository's last change — rather than implying a release.
Do keep contact in the bottom key row, right-aligned, rather than in a section of its own.
Do keep the desk at one fixed size and let long pages scroll inside the glass.
donts: Don't add a shadow that implies something floats, or a glow anywhere on the case. The pilot lens is flat; the phosphor is the only light.
Don't use blue for text, magenta for anything but the route key, or any pure primary.
Don't put a border radius inside the glass.
Don't replace the displacement map with a photo of a monitor, or a CSS bevel pretending to be plastic.
Don't ship JavaScript, a cookie, an analytics tag or a third-party font request.
Don't name a technology on the projects page. The list is about what things do.
Don't let a fixed glass height trap content on a phone.
Do not add a case, a bezel, a radius or a background behind the glass: the tube is the window.
Do not put a url() filter on anything that contains a link: it separates the paint from the hit box.
